newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European markets bask in warm glow from U.S..
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European markets bask in warm glow from U.S..

text.p: European shares took heart from Wall Street's strong close and were showing solid gains by midday on Monday, while the dollar softened against the mark as the chance of any early rise in U.S. interest rates receded.

The markets on both sides of the Atlantic were encouraged by the U.S. jobs report for February which on Friday showed little upward pressure on wages, despite a bigger-than-expected rise in the number of new jobs created.
The Dow Jones industrial index closed up 56.19 points at 7,000.89 on Friday and U.S. bonds rose, too.
Economists and traders concluded that the jobs report had not given the U.S. Federal Reserve cause to raise interest rates soon to check the threat of inflation.
Any rise in rates could sorely test the global bull market in shares which has pushed valuations to record after record recently.
Investors in shares fear higher interest rates as they harm companies profitability by rising the cost of borrowing. They also make alternative investments more attractive.
By 1145 gmt, London's FTSE index of leading blue chip shares was up 15.4 points, at 4,435.7, while in Paris the CAC-40 index was up 12.94 points at 2,721.22.

Germany's DAX index was up 65.56 points, almost two percent, at 3,4241.76, a new trading record. Most of the gains reflected the market, which had closed before Friday's U.S. jobs data, playing catch-up with the gains made elsewhere before the weekend. London and Paris both closed at record levels.
The DAX-Ibis index of electronic trading was up 20.23 points at 3,439.74 on Monday.
Leading London blue chips shares moved further into record territory, lifted by bullish comments from the Bank of England as well as Wall Street, dealers said.
Gilts also advanced after Bank of England Governor Eddie George said he believed the government could reach its 2.5 percent inflation target this year.

"He raised the question about whether it could be sustained, but up until now, he didn't even think it was a target that could be reached," one London share dealer said of George's forecast. "I think the chance of an early rate increase has receded quite significantly."
Sterling slipped in the wake of George's comments, which was broadly supportive of shares in major exporting companies.
British February producer price inflation was in line with expectations at 1.3 percent and one analyst said the data showed inflation was "very tame at the moment."
In Paris, French shares advanced from support just above the 2,700 level after opening below Friday's record close.
Traders said the market was supported by Wall Street's latest rise and that they expect U.S. markets to continue climbing.
"The market is consolidating. Wall Street was in good form last Friday," one broker in Paris said.

In currencies at midday, the dollar remained lower than Friday's close but was close to its opening levels as economists looked to this week's raft of U.S. data to provide further clues to the health of the U.S. economy.

The modest hourly earnings growth in the U.S. jobs report on Friday suggested a benign inflation outlook, analysts said. That reduced chances of an imminent interest rate rise and pulled the dollar from highs above 1.72 marks set initially after news of a big rise in non-farm jobs.
At 1145 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7091 compared with 1.7182 late on Friday.

Chartists saw the dollar consolidating above 1.70 after the retreat from Friday's highs and pegged support at 1.7050 marks. Analysts said it was likely to remain stuck in a narrow trading range about current levels later today.

"Late Friday's trade was dominated by unwinding of long dollar positions and the shift in the yield spreads shows changes in rate expectations were partly responsible," said Joe Prendergast, foriegn exchange strategist at Merrill Lynch.
The dollar was trading at 121.83 against the yen, down slightly from late last week.
CURRENCIES AT 1145 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7091 marks and 121.83 yen compared with 1.7182 marks and 121.94 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS 1145 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 15.4 points at 4,435.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 12.94 points at 2,721.22.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 65.56 points at 3,441.76 points.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1145 GMT
Gold fixed at $349.90 an ounce in London compared with $349.05 at the European close on Friday.
